PDD Holdings stock faces a tougher Temu test before Q3 results
sum: PDD Holdings is entering its next earnings checkpoint with investors balancing a lower valuation against rising costs around Temu. In an analysis updated October 30, TIKR said Deutsche Bank upgraded PDD from Hold to Buy after the October 29 session, while keeping its 105 US dollar price target. The report linked the more constructive rating to the share price rather than to a new earnings forecast.

TIKR also described the European compliance burden as an important part of the debate. The European Commission had accepted Temu's five-measure plan for addressing a Digital Services Act breach tied to a 200 million euro fine. The plan includes an interim risk assessment, while the broader case remains a source of execution and cost pressure for PDD's international marketplace.

Management commentary cited by TIKR points to heavier investment in platform governance. Co-Chairman and Co-CEO Zhao Jiazhen said PDD had introduced more than 150 trust and safety measures and launched more than 50 targeted initiatives in June. Financial Director Jun Liu reported non-GAAP research and development expense of 4.3 billion renminbi in the second quarter, up 40 percent, while non-GAAP operating expenses reached 31 percent of revenue compared with 29 percent a year earlier.

That spending comes as the company expands beyond its China marketplace. TIKR said management had acknowledged a significant shift in global regulatory and compliance conditions, while the rollout of first-party brands had taken longer than originally expected. The analysis also noted the European Union's 3 euro charge on low-value parcels, adding another variable for Temu's cross-border economics.

The earnings backdrop remains mixed. Second-quarter revenue was 112.36 billion renminbi, 1.36 percent below the consensus cited by TIKR, although adjusted earnings per share of 19.33 renminbi exceeded expectations by 5.34 percent. TIKR said PDD had missed revenue estimates in four consecutive quarters, with the shortfalls ranging from 0.42 percent to 2.90 percent.

For the third quarter, analysts cited by TIKR expected revenue of about 116 billion renminbi, representing growth of about 7 percent. A result at or above that level would improve the case that the valuation discount reflects temporary pressure.

sum: Alibaba Group Holding Limited BABA, JD.com, Inc. JD and PDD Holdings Inc. PDD are trading higher Monday after a report that China’s central bank and securities regulator will meet to discuss tools designed to support the country’s capital market.
- Alibaba stock is trading at elevated levels. What should traders watch with BABA?
China Regulators, Central Bank to Meet on Stock Market Support Measures

According to Bloomberg, the People’s Bank of China will meet with the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the China Securities Regulatory Commission and major banks on Monday to study how to improve a relending program for share buybacks and stake increases. Bloomberg cited a report Sunday from Cailian, which cited people in the industry. Some securities firms and funds have received notices about the meeting, according to the 21st Century Business Herald, as cited by Bloomberg. The newspaper said industry participants speculated that the meeting was likely preparation by financial regulators for further action to stabilize the market.
The Meeting Follows China’s Worst Month for Stocks in More Than a Decade

Bloomberg said a state-backed effort would add to steps China took last month to stabilize its equity market. Those measures have so far proved insufficient, Bloomberg reported, against the backdrop of a weak domestic economy and doubts over AI earnings, with Chinese stocks suffering their worst month in more than a decade. The CSI 300 Index fell into a bear market in October, dropping 8.5% and falling for a record 12 straight weeks. Bloomberg also noted that China’s official manufacturing and non-manufacturing purchasing managers’ indexes fell back into contraction in October.

NVDA Stock In For ‘Very, Very Fast’ Rally: Analysts Shrug Off Price-Hike Buzz Ahead Of Most-Watched Earnings Report
sum: Shares of Nvidia, Inc. (NVDA) rose nearly 1% in premarket trading on Tuesday, attempting to rebound from a seven-session rout as analysts argued that potential price increases for its newest AI systems should not derail demand and could strengthen an already bullish earnings setup.
NVDA stock fell 3% on Monday but remains up 4% for August, putting it on track for its strongest monthly performance since May.

Nvidia could reportedly raise prices for its Blackwell and Rubin systems as soaring memory costs push up production expenses. However, Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold said that a potential 15% increase would make sense given the amount of high-bandwidth memory packed into the platforms. “15% really doesn’t seem all that demanding,” Leopold said, adding that an even larger increase is possible.

Each Blackwell and Rubin GPU is paired with eight HBM stacks, each containing 12 layers of DRAM. Nvidia has also spent years locking in memory supplies through long-term agreements with multiple suppliers, potentially cushioning the effect of rising costs.

Still, Leopold cautioned that higher list prices may not translate directly into higher prices for major customers. “The public prices may go up by 15%, but that doesn’t mean contracted prices are reflecting that same amount,” he said.

Wall Street is bracing for another enormous quarter from Nvidia on Wednesday. Fiscal.ai projects revenue of $91.48 billion, more than double the year-earlier figure, with adjusted earnings of $2.07 per share and EBITDA of $61.83 billion.

Koyfin’s estimates are slightly higher at $92.07 billion in revenue, $2.09 in adjusted earnings and $61.99 billion in EBITDA. This would represent sequential growth of 13% in revenue and EBITDA and 12% in earnings.

sum: China's biggest artificial intelligence spender is leading a sharp retreat in U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks even as American large caps push higher, raising questions about whether heavy cloud spending is becoming a liability rather than an advantage.

Selling in U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks is landing hardest on the group’s biggest artificial intelligence spender, even as American large caps edge higher. Alibaba Group (NYSE:BABA | BABA Price Prediction) shares are down 5% to $103.67 in morning trading, a slide that puts the e-commerce and cloud giant at the front of the China tech retreat.

Meanwhile, JD.com (NASDAQ:JD) stock is down 4% to $25.65, a decline that trails the drop in Alibaba stock by a narrow margin. PDD Holdings (NASDAQ:PDD) shares are down 4% to $78.21, a move that lands in step with JD.com. That tight cluster among Alibaba, JD.com and PDD shares stands out while American buyers are otherwise buying into equities.

Among funds, the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (NYSEARCA:KWEB) is down 3% to $23.53. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.5% to $772.84. Thus, U.S. large-caps are holding up better than the KWEB ETF, BABA stock, JD stock, and PDD stock today.

Alibaba, JD.com and PDD shares are falling by similar amounts alongside the China internet fund while the S&P 500 tracker is higher. That pattern shows the selling spread across U.S.-listed Chinese internet stocks as a group, with the pressure landing on marketplace, direct retail and discount commerce models alike.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is the chip supplier at the center of a Reuters report published in the prior session. Citing two people familiar with the matter, Reuters said ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent had placed large orders. The focus was an NVIDIA workstation chip that can still be sold to Chinese buyers under U.S. export limits. The news service also reported that NVIDIA may be able to fill only a small share of those orders. That leaves open whether the story bears on Alibaba’s heavy artificial intelligence spending.

PDD Holdings Inc Stock (PDD) Moved Up by 3.08% on Oct 5: Facts Behind the Movement
sum: PDD Holdings Inc (PDD) moved up by 3.08%. The Software & IT Services sector is up by 1.04%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Microsoft Corp (MSFT) up 1.51%; Meta Platforms Inc (META) up 2.42%; Oracle Corp (ORCL) up 1.06%.

PDD Holdings experienced a notable upward move accompanied by heightened intraday volatility, primarily driven by a broader sentiment recovery across Chinese consumer discretionary and technology ADRs. Following an extended selloff that brought the stock near multi-year valuation lows, bargain-hunting and technical short-covering emerged near key technical support zones. Investors are recalibrating their expectations for Chinese cross-border and domestic e-commerce platforms amid ongoing macroeconomic stabilization efforts in China and a sector-wide rebound.

From a fundamental perspective, market participants are increasingly weighing PDD's strategic investment cycle against its deeply compressed valuation multiples. The company has committed substantial capital toward upgrading its merchant ecosystem, strengthening its domestic supply chain infrastructure, and absorbing rising international compliance and logistical costs for its Temu platform. While these strategic initiatives have pressured near-term operating margins and quarterly net earnings, the stock's valuation discount relative to historical averages and its massive net cash balance—representing a major fraction of its total market capitalization—are attracting value-oriented institutional investors.

Intraday trading dynamics further highlight institutional portfolio realignments as market participants assess the long-term payoff of PDD's global expansion against near-term regulatory and margin headwinds. Despite cross-border trade policy shifts and fierce domestic price competition, PDD continues to generate robust core cash flows supported by a resilient balance sheet. Today's upward movement underscores growing market recognition of an asymmetric risk-reward profile, where heavy near-term investment spend is increasingly priced into the stock, leaving room for valuation recovery upon operational stabilization.

items.t: US Stocks Wild Night: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Plunges Over 5%, Meta Surges 11%
sum: US equities staged a dramatic reversal on the first trading day of July. Just one session after chip stocks enjoyed a collective rally, market sentiment abruptly soured, triggering a fierce sell-off in the semiconductor sector that sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbling more than 5% intraday. In stark contrast, internet software giants led by Meta surged powerfully, while Chinese ADRs extended their rebound with broad-based gains.

As of 23:05 ET on July 1, the three major US indices gradually recovered after opening lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 managed to turn positive, while the Nasdaq Composite significantly narrowed its losses after falling nearly 1% earlier in the session. This intraday reversal underscores the intense tug-of-war between bulls and bears.

Just one session earlier on June 30, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had closed more than 3% higher, with memory chip maker SanDisk surging nearly 7% and Marvell Technology jumping over 7%, painting a broadly optimistic picture. Yet merely a day later, the same index plunged over 5%, completely wiping out the prior day's gains.

At the individual stock level, the carnage was severe. Teradyne tumbled over 10%, ranking among the worst-performing index constituents. Legacy chip giant Intel (INTC) cratered more than 7%. Lithography leader ASML (ASML) slumped over 6%. Marvell Technology, TSMC (TSM), GlobalFoundries (GFS), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and ARM all suffered substantial declines.

Memory chip stocks were hit especially hard. SanDisk plunged over 10%, Micron Technology (MU) dropped more than 8%, and Western Digital (WDC) fell over 7%. This marked an extreme reversal from the prior session's red-hot rally in memory names.

While the semiconductor sector was awash in red, internet and software giants carved out an independent trajectory. With the exception of recently high-flying Nvidia (NVDA), which declined, the so-called "Magnificent Seven" rose in unison. Meta (META) delivered a particularly stunning performance, with shares skyrocketing over 11% — an exceptionally rare move for a mega-cap tech stock — signaling that market capital is rapidly rotating from richly valued semiconductor hardware into software and internet applications.
